title: Rigveda 1.153: To Mitra and Varuna
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 1.153: To Mitra and Varuna: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 1.153 is a hymn of 4 verses addressed to Mitra and Varuna. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 1, a collection of hymns by many families of poets. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 117v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 1.153.1-4 (aṣṭaka 2, adhyāya 2, varga 23); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 117v
translation.original_text:
1yajā̍mahe vām ma̱haḥ sa̱joṣā̍ ha̱vyebhi̍r mitrāvaruṇā̱ namo̍bhiḥ | ghṛ̱tair ghṛ̍tasnū̱ adha̱ yad vā̍m a̱sme a̍dhva̱ryavo̱ na dhī̱tibhi̱r bhara̍nti ||
2prastu̍tir vā̱ṁ dhāma̱ na prayu̍kti̱r ayā̍mi mitrāvaruṇā suvṛ̱ktiḥ | a̱nakti̱ yad vā̍ṁ vi̱dathe̍ṣu̱ hotā̍ su̱mnaṁ vā̍ṁ sū̱rir vṛ̍ṣaṇā̱v iya̍kṣan ||
3pī̱pāya̍ dhe̱nur adi̍tir ṛ̱tāya̱ janā̍ya mitrāvaruṇā havi̱rde | hi̱noti̱ yad vā̍ṁ vi̱dathe̍ sapa̱ryan sa rā̱taha̍vyo̱ mānu̍ṣo̱ na hotā̍ ||
4u̱ta vā̍ṁ vi̱kṣu madyā̱sv andho̱ gāva̱ āpa̍ś ca pīpayanta de̱vīḥ | u̱to no̍ a̱sya pū̱rvyaḥ pati̱r dan vī̱tam pā̱tam paya̍sa u̱sriyā̍yāḥ ||
translation.text:
1WE worship with our reverence and oblations you, Mitra Varuṇa, accordant, mighty, So that with us, ye Twain whose backs are sprinkled with oil, the priests with oil and hymns support you.
2Your praise is like a mighty power, an impulse: to you, Twain Gods, a well-formed hymn is offered, As the priest decks you, Strong Ones, in assemblies, and the prince fain to worship you for blessings.
3O Mitra-Varuṇa, Aditi the Milch-cow streams for the rite, for folk who bring oblation, When in the assembly he who worships moves you, like to a human priest, with gifts presented.
4So may the kine and heavenly Waters pour you sweet drink in families that make you joyful. Of this may he, the ancient House-Lord, give us. Enjoy, drink of the milk the cow provideth.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 117v (numbered 11v by the scribe) (OPenn image 119, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 1.152.7 ‹ā vām mitrāvaruṇā havya-juṣṭim›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 118r (numbered 12r by the scribe), begins in RV 1.154.1 ‹kam vīryāṇi pra vocam›. Verses 1.153.1-4 end on this page.
